questions.stem: An elderly woman on treatment for migraine presents with new-onset chest pain, without any previous history of angina /MI. The drug with which of the following mechanisms of action might have caused this presentation?
questions.solutionHtml:
5 HT agonist
  • Triptans and ergotamine act by stimulating  5HT 1B/1D receptor which acts on blood vessels causing vasoconstriction resulting in  coronary artery spasm resulting in angina like symptoms in patients so should never be used in patients with coronary artery disease.

questions.stem: A patient with pelvic fracture and trauma was given morphine for pain. Following which he develops respiratory difficulty. What could be the cause?

options.label: C
options.text: Co2 retention due to opioid use

questions.answerText: Co2 retention due to opioid use
questions.solutionHtml:
Co2 retention due to opioid use
  • The most likely cause of respiratory difficulty given in the clinical scenario above is CO2 retention due to opioid use, as the patient was administered morphine after head trauma.
  • Head injury is considered as a contraindication to morphine use because:
  • Morphine retains CO2 that increases intracranial pressure (ICP) and adds to the already increased ICP.
  • Therapeutic doses can result in marked respiratory depression.
  • Interferes with the assessment of progress by causing miosis, vomiting and altered mentation.
